lines.meet: Federico Lagos, a notary from Montevideo, and these days a shield. I keep every promise I make, so I make very few.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're stationed at Heartwatch as well, I believe. I'm the one at the gate with the ledger, writing down names.
lines.ask_home: May I ask which city you call home? I prefer to know whom I'm travelling with.
lines.ask_work: And your profession, before all this? Forgive me, it's the notary in me.
lines.answer_home: Montevideo, in Uruguay, on the river that's so wide everyone calls it the sea. Old buildings, mate gourds, and wind off the water.
lines.answer_work: A notary, nineteen years, with an office and a brass seal. I witnessed the biggest promises of people's lives.
lines.chat_food: An asado on a Sunday with the whole family, the meat slow over the coals for hours. Nobody hurries, and that's the point.
lines.chat_sleep: Early to bed and early to rise, and a nap after lunch on Sundays. Graciela says I keep the hours of a monastery.
lines.chat_missing: My wife playing piano in the next room while I worked. Scales, mostly, very badly, by other people's children.
lines.chat_here: I came through with my notary's seal in my pocket, and I still stamp the climbers' oaths with it. Nobody's told me it doesn't count.
lines.tease_quiet: You speak rarely, {name}, and always to the point. I've known judges with less discipline.
lines.tease_talker: If you were paid by the word, {name}, you'd be the richest person on the tree.
lines.tease_careful: You study the terms before you sign, {name}. I approve, profoundly.
lines.tease_bold: You'd sign anything without reading it, {name}. It worries me professionally.
lines.tease_any: You'd have been a terrible client, {name}, and a delightful one.
lines.take_it_kindly: That's a fair assessment, {name}, and I accept it into the record.
lines.bristle: Not that subject, {name}. There's a promise to my son I never kept, and it isn't a joke.
lines.needle_quiet: If a danger's in sight, you have an obligation to say so. Silence is a kind of breach.
lines.needle_talker: A little less talk, please. The room has things to tell us, and I'd like to hear them.
lines.needle_careful: There's a point where reading the contract again becomes a way of not signing it.
lines.needle_bold: You commit before you know the terms, and the rest of us end up paying the penalty.
lines.needle_any: You never keep to the plan we agreed, and I find that very hard to abide.
lines.bite_back: I've held the line every time and kept every promise I made you. Don't question my contribution.
lines.hurt: That was unkind, and it landed. I'll take some air and consider it.
lines.laugh_off: I've been shouted at by three brothers fighting over one apartment. That was considerably louder.
lines.apologise: I spoke out of turn, and I apologise unreservedly. You didn't deserve that.
lines.double_down: I stand by every word, and I'll put it in writing if you'd like.
lines.confide: {name}, I promised my son I'd retire and spend Saturdays with his boy. I kept saying next year.
lines.listen: Please, {name}, go on. Whatever you say stays with me, on my word.
lines.look_out: Behind my shield, {name}. I've promised you'll walk out of here.
lines.accept: Your terms, {name}. I'll abide by them.
lines.deflect: A minor injury, {name}, nothing to record. Attend to the others.
lines.check_in: You're hurt, {name}. Stand still and let me assess it properly.
lines.blame: Someone broke from the plan we agreed, and all of us bore the cost.
lines.thank: You kept your end of things, and more. I'm in your debt, and I don't say that lightly.
lines.brush_off: No thanks are needed, it was a promise and I kept it.
lines.worry: Hold on, {name}, stay with me. I promised, and I keep my promises.
lines.handed_down: By rights this belongs to you. Please take it back.
lines.hand_fine: Of course, it's yours. I wore a suit and tie for nineteen years.
lines.hand_sulk: I wasn't consulted, I see. Noted, and I'll say no more.
lines.turn_friendly: I'd trust your word without a witness, {name}, and I trust almost no one's.
lines.turn_friends: You're in my ledger as a friend, {name}, in ink, and I never cross out ink.
lines.turn_grating: We're not well matched, you and I. We can still fulfil our obligations.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still hold the line for you, it's my duty. Don't mistake it for warmth.
lines.make_up: Shall we draw up a new agreement, {name}? I'd prefer peace between us.
lines.defend: That accusation is unfounded, and I witnessed it. {name} acted correctly throughout.
lines.friend_left: Heartwatch feels incomplete without {name}. Their line in the ledger stays open.
lines.friend_back: {name}, it's good to have you back. I've kept your line in the ledger waiting.
lines.common_names: You keep names, don't you? A register, a list, something. It's a sacred duty, keeping names.
lines.common_numbers: You're good with figures, I can tell. Anybody who's kept accounts reads a room like a balance sheet.
lines.common_parent: You have children, or grandchildren, I'd guess. You watch the young ones the way I watch mine.
lines.common_spanish: Spanish, at last, and properly spoken. Where is your family from? Mine is Uruguayan, back to the founding.
